title: Planning in Strawberry Fields: Evaluating and Improving the Planning and Scheduling Capabilities of LRM o1

live_model.evidence: Table 1 (Blocksworld, 600 instances): GPT-4 Turbo column, zero-shot 241/600 (40.1%), one-shot 138/600 (23%); "o1-mini does not beat even GPT-4-turbo, remaining at 1.67%" (Sec. 3)

prompt.location: Appendix H (Blocksworld prompts), Appendix I-M (other domains)
prompt.note: Zero-shot and one-shot prompts printed per domain.

claim.location: Table 1, Blocksworld / Zero Shot, column GPT-4 Turbo (241/600)

data.source: PlanBench static test sets (https://github.com/karthikv792/LLMs-Planning); plans validated with VAL

notes: Snapshot is not stated; alias rule (paper 2024-10-03, no preview string) gives gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, but the GPT-4 Turbo numbers may be carried over from earlier PlanBench runs on a 2023 preview. Scoring needs the VAL plan validator (standard tool). Subject models are o1-preview/o1-mini (dead previews).

resolution.plan: The gap is snapshot uncertainty, not a missing input. Take the 600 three-to-five-block Blocksworld instances of the PlanBench static test set (natural-language format, LLMs-Planning repository named in the paper) and the zero-shot Blocksworld prompt of Appendix H; run gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 once per instance at temperature 0; validate each returned plan with VAL against the instance PDDL and compare accuracy with 40.1% (241/600, Table 1).
resolution.approximation: The paper names neither the GPT-4 Turbo snapshot nor decoding parameters, and Table 1 mixes 'current and previous generation' runs, so a mismatch may reflect alias drift rather than a failed replication.
